A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–K are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic-control benchmark experiments, policy ablations, collected-dataset experiments, and toy function-approximation results in Appendix J.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies, including revised Push-T results in Tables 12–13.

M1.justification: MIP's training and inference procedures, SF/RR variants, and model architectures are retained. Removing the unused Gaussian z sampling clause beneath Equation 4.1 does not change the zero-input regression procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Robomimic, Push-T, Kitchen, MetaWorld, Adroit, and LIBERO coverage and Appendix J toy tasks. No datasets, observation modalities, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged, including regression, Flow, policy variants, CTM, LMD, and VINN. Table 13 expands DiT/Transformer/UNet labels to their existing full architecture names; these are not new comparators.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation protocols, model capacities, training budgets, and sampling procedures remain unchanged. Tables 12–13 retain the same best-checkpoint and last-five-checkpoint reporting despite their revised Push-T values; no rerun or protocol change is documented.

E4.justification: The component, data-quality, architecture, scaling, action-chunk, loss-norm, multimodality, and manifold-adherence analyses are retained. The Push-T table revisions change benchmark scores without adding or redesigning an analysis.

E5.justification: Three-seed reporting and existing uncertainty reporting in Tables 14 and 18 and Appendix J remain unchanged. No additional runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: All 24 Push-T entries across Tables 12–13 change from 1.00/1.00 to differentiated best/average scores. For example, Sudeep-DiT Flow becomes 0.98/0.95 for state observations and 0.92/0.89 for images. Image-based Chi-UNet MIP becomes 0.83/0.78 versus regression's 0.90/0.85, replacing their previous tie. These revisions concern one retained task; other numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The expressivity theorem and Appendix H proofs, Appendix I linear-surrogate derivations, and Appendix K formal definitions are unchanged. The unused-variable cleanup near Equation 4.1 does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, four contributions, and discussion retain the same claims: stochasticity combined with supervised iteration explains the studied advantages, distribution fitting is less essential, and MIP broadly matches Flow.

C2.justification: The manifold-adherence and stochasticity explanations remain unchanged, as do qualifications about unresolved theoretical mechanisms and applicability beyond behavior cloning. Repaired cross-references introduce no new interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix J replaces example.com placeholders for the full report and code with specific paths in the project's GitHub repository. This improves access information without adding implementation settings; the PDFs alone do not establish the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: Section 6, the bibliography, and the work's novelty positioning are unchanged. No cited research is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 repairs unresolved references in Section 3.4, Appendix F.2, and Appendix G, standardizes architecture names in Table 13, and makes small wording and acknowledgement edits. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned, including Figure 6 from page 11 to 10, Figure 8 from page 13 to 14, and Table 17 from page 36 to 37. Spacing and table layout receive limited adjustments; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Repaired references and specific Appendix J report/code links improve traceability. However, the revised Push-T tables are not reconciled with unchanged summary graphics: Table 12 now gives best regression and Flow scores of 0.95 and 0.98, implying roughly 0.97 relative performance, while Figure 2 still plots equal-height Push-T state bars. The unexplained numerical revisions and resulting reporting inconsistency make the net quality effect uncertain despite the documentation gains.
